newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end lower but liquidity tight.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end lower but liquidity tight.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed lower on Tuesday after the central bank expressed concerns over recent high short-term interest rates, dealers said.
The central bank had increased its issuance of negotiable certificates of deposits in April and traders said the move was aimed at mopping up liquidity to depress the bullish stock market.
The bank, denying the allegations, said recent short-term interest rates were high but said it would not inject funds into the banking system.
The overnight interbank rate ended at 7.011 percent against Monday's 7.181 close, with 30-day commercial paper also lower to 6.85 percent from 7.00.
Traders said liquidity would remain tight and expected the overnight interbank rate to move between 6.75-7.00 percent in the near term.
In the bond market, the 10-year 86/4 government bond yields were at 6.0900 percent against Monday's 6.0935 percent.
